clean-01-c1.quote: There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things.
clean-01-c1.claim: Phil Karlton's quip, "there are only two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation and naming things"

clean-01-c3.text: The Go Authors (2013). go fmt your code. The Go Blog (go.dev).
clean-01-c3.quote: Gofmt is a tool that automatically formats Go source code.
clean-01-c3.claim: Modern languages ship with auto-formatters: gofmt for Go

clean-02-c1.quote: If you have to spend effort into looking at a fragment of code to figure out what it's doing, then you should extract it into a function and name the function after that “what”.
clean-02-c1.claim: The technique is called extract function: when a piece of logic forms a coherent step, give it a name and pull it out.

clean-02-c3.quote: My general reaction to flag arguments is to avoid them. Rather than use a flag argument, I prefer to define separate methods.
clean-02-c3.claim: Two functions saveDraft and publishUser beat one parametrized monster.

clean-03-c1.text: Robert C. Martin (2000). Design Principles and Design Patterns. Object Mentor.
clean-03-c1.quote: A module should be open for extension but closed for modification.
clean-03-c1.claim: O, Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification (add new behavior by adding new types, not editing old ones).

clean-03-c1.text: Robert C. Martin (2000). Design Principles and Design Patterns. Object Mentor.
clean-03-c1.quote: Subclasses should be substitutable for their base classes.
clean-03-c1.claim: L, Liskov Substitution: subtypes must be usable wherever their parents are.

clean-03-c2.text: Bill Venners (2003). Orthogonality and the DRY Principle: A Conversation with Andy Hunt and Dave Thomas. Artima Developer.
clean-03-c2.quote: DRY says that every piece of system knowledge should have one authoritative, unambiguous representation.
clean-03-c2.claim: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself): every piece of knowledge should have a single, authoritative representation.

clean-03-c3.quote: It's a statement that some capability we presume our software needs in the future should not be built now because “you aren't gonna need it”.
clean-03-c3.claim: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It): don't build things until you actually need them.

clean-04-c1.text: Martin Fowler (2018). Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code. martinfowler.com.
clean-04-c1.quote: This is the second edition of the book, published late in 2018. The first edition came out in 1999.
clean-04-c1.claim: The classic reference is Martin Fowler's Refactoring (1999), cataloging dozens of named moves: Extract Function, Inline Variable, Replace Conditional with Polymorphism, Introduce Parameter Object.

clean-04-c2.quote: A code smell is a surface indication that usually corresponds to a deeper problem in the system.
clean-04-c2.claim: A code smell is a surface symptom of deeper trouble.

clean-04-c3.quote: Technical Debt is a metaphor, coined by Ward Cunningham, that frames how to think about dealing with this cruft, thinking of it like a financial debt.
clean-04-c3.claim: Ward Cunningham coined technical debt as a metaphor: short-term shortcuts that you'll pay back later, with interest.

clean-05-c2.quote: the Test Pyramid due to Mike Cohn, when he described it in his 2009 book Succeeding with Agile.
clean-05-c2.claim: The test pyramid (Mike Cohn) prescribes a healthy mix of test types.

clean-05-c3.text: Martin Fowler (2023). Test Driven Development. martinfowler.com.
clean-05-c3.quote: Test-Driven Development (TDD) is a technique for building software that guides software development by writing tests. It was developed by Kent Beck in the late 1990's as part of Extreme Programming.
clean-05-c3.claim: Test-Driven Development (TDD), popularized by Kent Beck, follows a tight cycle: red (write a failing test), green (write the simplest code that passes), refactor (clean up while tests stay green).

clean-05-c3.quote: Test coverage is a useful tool for finding untested parts of a codebase. Test coverage is of little use as a numeric statement of how good your tests are.
clean-05-c3.claim: It's a useful diagnostic but a terrible target.
